about: Simple landmark reconstructions, Rome c. AD 100 (build-landmarks.mjs). angle: degrees from east, anticlockwise, of the length axis, pointing to the front where a kit has one. size: [length, width] metres.

landmarks.title: Flavian Amphitheatre (Colosseum)
landmarks.note: Outer ellipse 189 × 156 m, arena 87 × 55 m, 48 m high (published); placed and turned by the mapped outline. Four tiers of seating stepped down to an open arena.

landmarks.title: Ludus Magnus (gladiators' school)
landmarks.note: Barracks round a courtyard with a small arena, by the mapped outline of the excavated part. Height a guess.

landmarks.title: Arch of Titus
landmarks.note: Published size and height, on its standing position.

landmarks.title: Basilica Julia
landmarks.note: Published plan 101 × 49 m, by the mapped outline; heights a guess.

landmarks.title: Basilica Aemilia
landmarks.note: About 100 × 29 m by the mapped outline; heights a guess.

landmarks.title: Curia Julia (Senate house, Domitian's rebuilding)
landmarks.note: The standing building is Diocletian's on the same plan: 27 × 18 m, 21 m high.

landmarks.title: Temple of Castor and Pollux
landmarks.note: Podium about 50 × 32 m and 7 m high (published); columns 12.5 m. Faces the Forum square.

landmarks.title: Temple of the Deified Julius
landmarks.note: By the mapped podium; height a guess.

landmarks.title: Temple of Concord
landmarks.note: Transverse cella, wider (45 m) than deep, facing down the Forum, by the mapped podium (whose outline is near square, so the facing is a judgement); height a guess.

landmarks.title: Temple of Saturn
landmarks.note: Podium 40 × 22 m and about 9 m high; the standing columns are 11 m. Faces north-east across the Vicus Iugarius to the Forum, as the mapped podium runs.

landmarks.title: Temple of Vespasian and Titus
landmarks.note: By the mapped podium; columns 15.2 m.
landmarks.position: OpenStreetMap relation/1767603 (Tempio di Vespasiano e Tito)

landmarks.title: Temple of Vesta
landmarks.note: Round temple about 15 m across; height a guess.

landmarks.title: House of the Vestals
landmarks.note: Rooms round a long court, at the size of the mapped outline (about 104 × 55 m); height a guess.

landmarks.title: Regia
landmarks.note: Small irregular building; a block of about its size.

landmarks.title: Temple of Jupiter Optimus Maximus (Capitoline)
landmarks.note: Podium about 62 × 54 m (published; estimates vary). Placed at the Pleiades point, which is only good to about 2 km, and checked against the remains under Palazzo Caffarelli; faced south. Domitian's rebuilding after AD 80.

landmarks.title: Forum of Caesar
landmarks.note: Colonnaded square 160 × 75 m (published), by the mapped outline.

landmarks.title: Temple of Venus Genetrix
landmarks.note: By the mapped podium at the head of the Forum of Caesar; height a guess.

landmarks.title: Forum of Augustus
landmarks.note: Colonnades and exedrae round the square, about 125 × 118 m with them, by the mapped outline; the 33 m fire wall behind is drawn at the colonnades' height.

landmarks.title: Temple of Mars Ultor
landmarks.note: By the mapped podium; columns 17.7 m (published).

landmarks.title: Forum of Nerva (Forum Transitorium)
landmarks.note: A long walled square, 120 × 45 m, by the mapped outline; its columns stood against the walls.

landmarks.title: Temple of Minerva (Forum of Nerva)
landmarks.note: At the head of the Forum of Nerva, by the mapped remains; size and height a guess.

landmarks.title: Temple of Peace (Templum Pacis)
landmarks.note: A garden square of about 135 × 110 m inside porticoes. The mapped outline covers only the excavated part, so the published size is set on its centre and axis.

landmarks.title: Pantheon (Agrippa's, restored by Domitian)
landmarks.note: Drawn on the plan of Hadrian's rebuilding (c. AD 113-125), which stands on the same site and faces the same way; the Pantheon of AD 100 was Domitian's restoration of Agrippa's, and its form is uncertain.

landmarks.title: Saepta Julia
landmarks.note: Porticoes round a long enclosure, about 310 × 120 m (published), set east of the Pantheon as Platner describes it; position about 50 m.

landmarks.title: Baths of Agrippa
landmarks.note: The mapped fragment is the round hall (Arco della Ciambella); the bath block about it is a guess, about 100 × 80 m.

landmarks.title: Stadium of Domitian
landmarks.note: Piazza Navona keeps the arena (about 258 × 54 m, the mapped square); the stands round it about 26 m deep (outer size about 275 × 106 m, published). Curved end to the north. Height a guess.

landmarks.title: Theatre of Pompey
landmarks.note: Cavea about 150 m across (published), facing east. The Pleiades point is the line of Via di Grotta Pinta, which follows the curve; the centre is set 25 m east of it. The Temple of Venus Victrix crowns the cavea. Height a guess.

landmarks.title: Porticus of Pompey
landmarks.note: The garden portico behind the stage, about 180 × 135 m (published), reaching east to the Largo Argentina temples.

landmarks.title: Baths of Nero
landmarks.note: Between the Stadium of Domitian and the Pantheon, under Palazzo Madama, as Platner places them; about 190 × 120 m. Position about 50 m; size and height a guess.

landmarks.title: Odeum of Domitian
landmarks.note: South of the stadium; the curved front of Palazzo Massimo follows its cavea, so the stage faced north. About 100 m across; height a guess.

landmarks.title: Largo Argentina, Temple B
landmarks.note: Round temple by its mapped podium; height a guess.

landmarks.title: Largo Argentina, Temple C
landmarks.note: By its mapped podium; height a guess.

landmarks.title: Largo Argentina, Temple D
landmarks.note: By its mapped podium; height a guess.

landmarks.title: Porticus of Octavia
landmarks.note: Porticoes 119 × 132 m (published) behind the standing propylon, which is mapped; the precinct is set on it.

landmarks.title: Mausoleum of Augustus
landmarks.note: About 89 m across (mapped). The drum and the planted mound above it are drawn as stepped tiers; heights after the published reconstructions (about 42 m), a guess.

landmarks.title: Ara Pacis Augustae (original site)
landmarks.note: The enclosure, 11.6 × 10.6 m (published), at its original site from Pleiades (it now stands by the Mausoleum).

landmarks.title: Obelisk of the Horologium Augusti
landmarks.note: The obelisk (21.8 m) on its base, at the Pleiades point.

landmarks.title: Iseum Campense (sanctuary of Isis)
landmarks.note: The long court of the sanctuary of Isis, between the Saepta and the Porticus Divorum, by a traced reconstruction (its east and west porticoes); rebuilt by Domitian after the fire of AD 80. Height a guess.

landmarks.title: Temple of Isis
landmarks.note: At the north end of the court, facing down it to the Serapeum (just east of Santa Maria sopra Minerva, as the remains are placed); size and height a guess.

landmarks.title: Serapeum
landmarks.note: The hall at the south end of the sanctuary, under Santo Stefano del Cacco, by a traced reconstruction; its apsed court is drawn as one hall. Height a guess.

landmarks.title: Porticus Divorum
landmarks.note: Domitian's portico for the deified Vespasian and Titus on the site of the Villa Publica, about 240 × 78 m, by a traced reconstruction. The OpenStreetMap and Pleiades point for it lies about 50 m further east, so the position is good to about that. Height a guess.

landmarks.title: Theatre of Balbus
landmarks.note: Cavea about 95 m across (published), facing east to the Crypta, set with its back on the back of the traced outline (which is 113 m across); the orientation is disputed. Height a guess.

landmarks.title: Crypta Balbi
landmarks.note: The portico behind the theatre's stage, about 114 × 90 m, by a traced reconstruction; its remains are under the Crypta Balbi museum. Height a guess.

landmarks.title: Porticus Philippi
landmarks.note: The portico round the Temple of Hercules Musarum, about 92 × 50 m, by a traced reconstruction, moved 13 m north-west to clear the Porticus of Octavia at its published size. Height a guess.

landmarks.title: Temple of Hercules Musarum
landmarks.note: A round temple inside the Porticus Philippi, at the traced position (marked approximate), moved with the portico. Height a guess.

landmarks.title: Temple of Juno Regina
landmarks.note: One of the two temples inside the Porticus of Octavia, by a traced reconstruction; height a guess.

landmarks.title: Temple of Jupiter Stator
landmarks.note: The other temple inside the Porticus of Octavia, by a traced reconstruction; height a guess.

landmarks.title: Temple of Neptune in Circo
landmarks.note: On the north side of the Circus Flaminius, facing it; the traced position is marked approximate. Size and height a guess.

landmarks.title: Temple of Hercules Custos
landmarks.note: On the north side of the Circus Flaminius, facing it, by a traced reconstruction. Size and height a guess.

landmarks.title: Temple of Minerva Chalcidica
landmarks.note: Domitian's temple east of the Iseum, by a traced reconstruction; which way it faced is a judgement. Height a guess.

landmarks.title: Baths of Titus
landmarks.note: A bath block of about 120 × 110 m at the centre of the zone drawn round it; size and height a guess.

landmarks.title: Temple of the Deified Claudius: terrace
landmarks.note: The terrace, about 200 × 175 m, with porticoes round it, in the zone drawn round it; height a guess.

landmarks.title: Temple of the Deified Claudius
landmarks.note: The temple on its terrace; size a guess.

landmarks.title: Castra Praetoria
landmarks.note: Walls of about 440 × 380 m (published), turned by the zone drawn round the camp, about 5 m high before the Aurelian heightening; barrack rows inside are a guess.

landmarks.title: Circus of Gaius and Nero
landmarks.note: About 540 × 90 m, running east-west along the south flank of today's St Peter's, with the obelisk on its spine; on the Pleiades point. Height a guess.
